newsitem.title: USA: House Democrats protest Bank committee schedule.
newsitem.headline: House Democrats protest Bank committee schedule.

text.p: Democrats on the House Banking Committee on Tuesday objected to a schedule for consideration of bank reform legislation adopted by Committee Republicans.
The Democrats charged that the schedule, which would allow meetings to propose amendments to bank legislation only in the full Banking Committee, could make it more difficult to enact the proposals.

"If we're going to be in the best possible position to deal with the issues we have to have thorough hearings on all aspects of it," Rep Bruce Vento, Democract from Minnesota, said at a banking subcommittee hearing on Tuesday.
Abandoning the usual procedure "puts us in a weaker position on the floor," Vento said. "This committee has had some big challenges in bringing regulatory measures to the floor."

Rep Marge Roukema, chairwoman of the subcommittee on financial institutions, responded that the schedule was designed to allow full consideration of complex legislation that cut across the jurisdiction of several subcommittees.
